sources.title: Moonshot API pricing page bundle, archived November 6, 2025
sources.publisher: Moonshot AI; preserved by Internet Archive
sources.evidence: Reopened the archived launch-day page bundle on October 27, 2026. It explicitly identifies kimi-k2-thinking-turbo as a high-speed version of kimi-k2-thinking with 256k context, establishing named model lineage. The K2 section supports ToolCalls and excludes vision. Its additional same-model-parameters wording names kimi-k2-turbo-preview; that separate sibling statement is not used to prove Thinking Turbo checkpoint identity.

sources.title: Kimi Code CLI: Interaction and Input
sources.evidence: Explicitly names kimi-k2-thinking-turbo as a model that always uses thinking mode and cannot disable it.

sources.title: Kimi-K2-Thinking model card
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27, 2026. The developer model summary separately publishes nominal 1T total and 32B activated parameters for Kimi K2 Thinking, with MoE architecture, 384 experts and 8 selected experts per token. The card describes native INT4 quantization/QAT for inference speed; it does not describe a pruned or distilled Turbo architecture or identify a separate Turbo checkpoint.

sources.title: Coding with Kimi K2: Top 6 Agents & Setup Guides
sources.evidence: The December 22, 2025 first-party guide explicitly recommends kimi-k2-thinking-turbo for speed and describes it as optimized for high-speed generation, reaching up to 100 tokens/s. This later serving-oriented description corroborates the launch-day named high-speed-version relationship; it does not report pruning, distillation, expert expansion or added modalities.

name.note: Readable form of the exact first-party kimi-k2-thinking-turbo endpoint name.

developer.note: Moonshot publishes and announces this exact API model.

family.note: The developer groups the exact Thinking Turbo endpoint within the Kimi K2 series; normalize to kimi-k2.

release_date.note: Official release log explicitly dates both K2 Think and its turbo version to November 6; this is not inferred from the standard checkpoint date.

open_weights.note: The standard Thinking weights are public, but no accessed first-party source establishes exact checkpoint equivalence for the hosted Turbo variant. High-speed version alone does not prove identical released weights; clear the baseline true.

license.note: Modified MIT is verified for standard K2 Thinking weights, not this exact hosted Turbo model. No established checkpoint mapping supports transferring that license, and missing mapping does not establish proprietary weights.

parameters_b.note: Nominal total-parameter inference from explicit developer lineage: the official launch-day API documentation identifies this exact endpoint as the high-speed version of kimi-k2-thinking, whose developer card reports 1T total parameters. Record that published nominal size as 1000B, without claiming a tensor census or byte-identical hosted checkpoint. Fresh searches and reopened later first-party materials found no Turbo pruning, distillation, expert expansion or added-modality disclosure that would defeat the inference; do not rely on the separate K2 Turbo Preview same-parameters statement.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal activated-parameter inference from the same explicitly identified K2 Thinking model: its developer card separately reports 32B activated parameters. The high-speed Turbo description and later speed guide disclose no altered expert selection or model structure; retain the developer convention as 32B rather than equating active with total, counting packed INT4 storage, or claiming a Turbo-specific exact per-token census.

architecture.note: Architecture inference coupled to the nominal parameter inference: Moonshot explicitly identifies Turbo as the high-speed version of Kimi K2 Thinking, whose model card specifies Mixture-of-Experts. Fresh first-party searches found no Turbo structural-change disclosure that would defeat this named-model lineage; this does not establish byte-identical deployed weights.

context_window.note: The archived launch-day API pricing page explicitly advertises 256k for this exact endpoint, corroborated as 262144 in Moonshot CLI configuration for the same identifier. This is the documented historical context budget, not a larger checkpoint positional ceiling or a claim of current endpoint operation.

modalities.note: The historical K2 API documentation excludes vision and staff show exact Turbo text chat-completions/function calls. Retain text input and output; do not inherit image support from illustrative CLI capability flags.

reasoning.note: Exact-model first-party CLI guidance explicitly classifies Turbo as always thinking with no disable switch; the launch announcement also names reasoning support.

tool_call.note: The API pricing section and exact-model staff request explicitly establish tool/function calling.

description.value: High-speed Kimi K2 Thinking API variant for text reasoning and tool calling; the original Moonshot endpoint is deprecated.
description.note: Describe the specifically documented hosted variant and its lifecycle, avoiding unsupported transfer of standard-checkpoint long-horizon benchmarks.

patch.description: High-speed Kimi K2 Thinking API variant for text reasoning and tool calling; the original Moonshot endpoint is deprecated.
patch.notes: Historical Moonshot API speed variant, released November 6, 2025 and listed as deprecated since May 25, 2026. Its advertised 256K context is represented as 262144 tokens; always-thinking and tool calling are explicit. Parameter re-audit on October 27, 2026 accepts nominal 1T total/32B activated parameters through the official identification of this endpoint as the high-speed version of Kimi K2 Thinking and that named model's developer-published specification. Later first-party speed guidance corroborates this relationship; fresh searches found no Turbo-specific pruning, distillation, changed expert selection or added modalities. These are nominal model counts inferred from explicit lineage, not an exact tensor census, whole-service inventory or proof of byte-identical hosted weights. MoE architecture follows the same explicit lineage. Openness and license assessments are unchanged; a public standard Thinking weights link is not a verified Turbo checkpoint.

Kimi K2 Thinking developer-published nominal parameter specifications

summary: Parameter re-audit verified nominal 1000B total and 32B activated parameters, plus coupled MoE architecture, by combining the official exact-endpoint identification as a high-speed version of Kimi K2 Thinking with that named model's developer specifications. Reopened launch, model-card and later first-party sources and searched for structural changes; no Turbo-specific pruning, distillation or expert-selection change was found. Exact hosted checkpoint identity remains unproven and is not required for these labeled lineage inferences. Unrelated field assessments are preserved; openness and license remain unverified.
